mechanism_claims.claim_text: AMP 1003 directly perturbs bacterial membrane-associated functions, with source-local evidence from competitive inhibition, membrane potential/permeability, leakage, and morphology assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: AMP 1003 against MRSA ATCC 33591 and K. pneumoniae ATCC 700603

mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports membrane perturbation in the tested bacterial systems; it does not establish a single exclusive pore model or quantify all figure-image cells not present in structured source data.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AMP 1003 has non-membrane stress evidence including DNA interaction, ROS accumulation, and intracellular nucleic-acid/protein leakage assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: AMP 1003-treated MRSA ATCC 33591 and K. pneumoniae ATCC 700603

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=5:Fig. 5; xml:sec=8:AMP 1003 performing multiple antimicrobial mechanisms

mechanism_claims.limitations: These assays support multi-target stress context; they should not be promoted to a fully mapped intracellular target pathway.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Transcriptomic panels support a broader stress-response context involving membrane repair, DNA damage response, transporter, and metabolic pathways.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MRSA ATCC 33591 and K. pneumoniae ATCC 700603 under AMP 1003 treatment
mechanism_claims.limitations: Transcriptomic changes are contextual and concentration-dependent; they are not by themselves direct proof of a single lethal molecular target.

source_review_summary.overclaim_policy: Direct classes are assigned only to assays with source locators; transcriptomics is kept as supportive context.
